narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your total years of professional experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and the fact that you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (half have only 1–5 years), the model sees your mid-level tenure as aligning more with people who eventually move on. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in this organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction, as this range is common among those who depart rather than those who remain long-term. Finally, receiving external job opportunities strongly increased the likelihood of leaving, since most employees predicted to stay (77%) report receiving no such offers.

Taken together, these three elements created a clear signal that you are likely to leave. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore whether improved recognition, better training access, or clearer promotion paths could increase your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying more attractive before making any decisions. (248 words)
